To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the particle filter with rejection and resampling control, proposed in this paper, has better mixing properties than the particle filter with resampling control only; (b) the proposed particle filter enables unbiased estimation of marginal likelihoods; (c) the proposed method is computationally efficient and easy to implement.

(1) we present a new particle filter that uses rejection control to improve its performance, (2) we show that this particle filter enables unbiased estimation of its model evidence (the marginal likelihood), and (3) we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed particle filter in a number of experiments.

1) the particle filter with rejection sampling and resampling can be made into a consistent estimator of the marginal likelihood, 2) the particle filter without rejection sampling can be made into an unbiased estimator of the marginal density of a single observation (or a single batch of observations).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three questions: 1. What is the best way to combine rejection control with particle filtering, so as to minimize bias and variance?
the following two questions: (i) Can we use rejection control in particle filters? If yes, how can we do it in an unbiased manner?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the particle filter with rejection sampling and resampling is a very powerful tool for the estimation of the marginal density of the state vector.
the particle filter with rejection is an attractive method for sequential Monte Carlo methods.
the particle filter with rejection and resampling is the method of choice for sequential Monte Carlo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to obtain a particle filter with resampling and rejection control, which is able to estimate the normalizing constant of the target distribution without bias.
the particle filter with rejection sampling and the particle filter with partial rejection control can be combined to give a particle filter with unbiased estimation of the normalizing constant.

we have developed an unbiased particle filter that is able to handle a large class of non-standard models and that can be used to obtain unbiased estimators of the marginal likelihood and of the marginal density of the observations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the unbiased estimator of the marginal likelihood is a byproduct of the particle filter with rejection, and it can be computed in a straightforward manner.
rejection control can be used as a variance-reducing tool in particle filters, while at the same time enabling unbiased estimation of the model evidence.

, when using rejection control, the marginal likelihood can be estimated by the ratio of the average weight of the particles in the last iteration and the average weight in the initial iteration, up to a constant that is independent of the number of particles.
